findings.title: Preserve support for v1 protobuf messages in the codec
findings.why_it_matters: RPCs using messages generated by older versions of protoc-gen-go now fail to marshal or unmarshal with the default codec because those messages implement the v1 interface but not ProtoReflect. The previous codec accepted the v1 interface and adapted it internally. Accepting both interface versions and adapting v1 messages before using the new API preserves existing clients and servers.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept both protoadapt.MessageV1 and protoadapt.MessageV2 in Marshal and Unmarshal, converting v1 messages with protoadapt.MessageV2Of before passing them to the protobuf API; add a v1-only message round-trip test.
evidence: The diff changes the imported proto.Message from github.com/golang/protobuf/proto (v1 interface) to google.golang.org/protobuf/proto (v2 interface requiring ProtoReflect).

findings.title: Unwrap legacy status details before returning them
findings.why_it_matters: Callers retrieving a status detail generated with the older protobuf API now receive an internal v2 wrapper instead of their concrete message type, so existing type switches and type assertions fail. Previously DynamicAny converted the decoded message to the v1 representation, unwrapping legacy messages. Applying the same conversion to the newly decoded detail restores its original concrete type.
findings.suggested_fix: Append protoadapt.MessageV1Of(detail) to the result, and test a registered v1-only detail message through WithDetails and Details.
evidence: The previous ptypes.DynamicAny path calls ptypes.Empty, which converts the registered message via proto.MessageV1; protoadapt.MessageV1Of unwraps legacy v2 wrappers.

findings.title: Report the actual invalid load interval error
findings.why_it_matters: An invalid or missing load reporting interval now logs `invalid load_reporting_interval: <nil>`, concealing the reason the LRS response was rejected and making control-plane configuration failures harder to diagnose. The error passed to fmt.Errorf comes from the successful stream receive, rather than CheckValid. Capturing the validation error restores the diagnostic.
findings.suggested_fix: Bind the result of rInterval.CheckValid() to err in the if statement and include that error in the returned message.
